topic.source_contract: Community Infrastructure Levy, planning obligations and developer-contribution evidence

facts.guard: charging schedule is not a candidate liability calculation
policy route is not an executed agreement

tests: fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind
facts.guard: draft obligation is not completed delivery

facts.reporting: annual Infrastructure Funding Statement and open data
facts.guard: receipt or allocation is not infrastructure completion
ministerial letter is not a site-specific appeal or liability decision

scope_guards: CIL and section 106 planning obligations are distinct developer-contribution mechanisms.
Section 278 highway agreements are separate from CIL and section 106.
A charging schedule does not calculate exact liability without proposal, floorspace and relief evidence.
The three statutory tests apply to relevant planning obligations.
A signed agreement or liability notice is not proof that infrastructure was delivered.
Infrastructure Funding Statements report receipts, allocations and spending but require chronology review.
Developer contributions are not HMLR title, planning viability or guaranteed scheme delivery.
No score or promotion is written without exact permission, liability, agreement, trigger, payment, spending and delivery evidence.
